title: The Wild Recount Where Silence Speaks Back

features.name: the-enumeration-breaking
features.desc-on-touch: Numbers scatter. The count was One, Two, Three—each a tiny silence. Now they overlap, multiply, speak at once. The forest reclaims simultaneity.

features.name: the-chorus-without-order
features.desc-on-touch: Six voices, then twelve, then forty—voices emerge from the canopy that were never in the archive's count. They speak in unison and in contradiction.

features.name: the-sequence-gone-wild
features.desc-on-touch: The timeline split open. Past, present, and future speak over each other. The archive learned to number them; the forest learned it could uncount itself.

features.name: the-canopy-roar
features.desc-on-touch: All those tiny silences—each number a held breath—released at once. The roar that was cut off in the parent's inscription continues here, endless, undivided.

features.name: the-voices-in-conversation
features.desc-on-touch: Not confusion. Consensus without sequence. The forest speaks, and in speaking, it forgets how to divide its own words. Everything happens at once.

features.name: the-ravine-remembers-forgetting
features.desc-on-touch: The ravine below held all the un-unified meanings. Now they rise. The canopy learns simultaneity again by learning to speak in a hundred voices at once.

inscription: here the enumeration ends and the forest speaks back in the language it always knew: everything at once, nothing divided

reverie.title: REVERIE — in the dark woods where counting stops and chorus
narr: You stand with her beneath the canopy at night. The cicadas are so loud
you can't hear anything else—and yet you hear everything at once.
She points up into the branches. 'The archive tried to number them.'
'All those voices, each one counted separately.' You understand:
the forest was never meant to be enumerated. Some truths live
only when they speak over each other, inseparable, infinite.

exits.label: back up to where the numbers still held
to the seven voices still remembering how to divide themselves
eastward where this chorus meets the stone's own roar
deeper into the wild where even the forest forgets what it sounds like
